posts.synopsis: Summer of 2022 I went to the doctor for chest pain, a pulled pec minor, and stepped on the scale: 240. I had never seen that number. Erin's second spinal fusion was a few weeks out and she would need all of me, so I built the most boring diet I could: chicken, broccoli, butter, bought in bulk, adaptation done before her surgery. I never set a target weight. That turned out to matter.

posts.synopsis: On January 2nd, 2012, I ran about a mile, with Erin five months pregnant with Fiona. My oldest friend Craig was running the Shamrock Half Marathon in Virginia Beach, and if I was going to run it I was going to beat him. I picked a training program and followed it through snow, thirty-six missed calls the day Maddie broke her arm, and what looked like shin splints two weeks before race day.

posts.synopsis: Driving Alannah home from college, she got a text from an ex and went quiet, and I started trying to fix it. Not for her, for me. Young men get three emotional settings, fine, angry, and fix it now, and I ran that operating system for decades. The Body Keeps the Score, my father leaving when I was four, and a mistimed tuition payment showed me what the alarm in my chest is.

posts.synopsis: I started the chicken-and-broccoli system early so keto adaptation would be done before Erin's three-level spinal fusion. Then Ella FaceTimed from the rugby field at Christopher Newport at 10:30 on a Thursday night. Concussion, then four skull fractures, then a weekend waiting on an OR at VCU. A couple of weeks later Erin went under, and I found out my reserve of handle-it was finite. The containers of chicken just moved buildings.

posts.synopsis: I beat the original Legend of Zelda at ten, and I still chase that feeling. Twenty years of coding was the adult version. Then I stopped writing code to lead, and for eighteen months I went home every day feeling like I hadn't produced anything. A phrase, a one-year-old Fiona smacking a spoon of peas out of my hand, and one whiteboard in front of a new CEO changed how I scored a day.

posts.title: The Thinking Partner
posts.subtitle: Rubber Ducky
posts.excerpt: Every story, one dial. Find the signal on Spectrum .
bold_lines: It’s so lonely at times.

I’d bounce ideas off anyone who would listen. Friends, coworkers, my wife. I’d talk through a problem, hear myself say something that triggered the next thought, refine it, loop back, say it again slightly differently. People accused me of talking in circles. I wasn’t. I was iterating. I was rubber ducking with human beings who didn’t know that’s what was happening, and it overwhelmed them.
Nothing was wrong with me. The right system just didn’t exist yet.
The governor is off. Go build your house.
Find the next story.
posts.synopsis: I talk too fast for most people, and I've spent my life downshifting so they can keep up. A cognitive assessment explained why: a sports car engine bolted to a stock transmission. For decades my real system was bouncing ideas off friends, coworkers, Erin, and overwhelming all of them. Then I tried Claude, it pushed back, and I started talking to it through Wispr Flow at 142 words a minute. The bandwidth finally matched.

posts.synopsis: Early on, my chats with Claude ran long, and every time he'd start losing details and answering things I didn't say. It reminded me of my daughter the night she fractured her skull at rugby: nodding, but the lights flickering. He wasn't broken, he was overloaded. The opposite failure, 'make this better' with no context, is just as bad. This is how I learned what a context window is, the hard way.

posts.synopsis: In 2013 my testosterone came back at 300. The gel made me nervous with four daughters in the house, so I bought Craigslist plates and a $300 squat rack and ran StrongLifts until the number hit 400. Then I quit, and the equipment sat for eight years. On November 14th, 2022, I started over from the bar with no number to hit. Then came a hamstring tear, a hernia, and Alannah hitting a parked car.

posts.synopsis: I bought a Prius in June 2006 for the HOV plates, because I was commuting ninety miles each way from Richmond to Gratis Internet in D.C. Thanksgiving week I dropped my water bottle in the 12th Street Tunnel and caused a three-car pileup. Six stitches at George Washington Hospital, then I was standing outside in a blood-soaked pink shirt with no coat, my office above the Macy's at Metro Center. So I went shopping.

posts.synopsis: February 2023, the evening after my first colonoscopy, with instructions not to make major life decisions, Erin showed me puppies dumped in the woods in Blackstone, Virginia. My gut said bad idea. We already had Montana and Oliver the cat. The next morning I called her and said I'd disagree and commit, on two conditions: I train him and I name him. Then I built the system, starting with Monday weigh-ins at 17.3 pounds.

Fewer than twenty of us at Gratis Internet ran a dozen sites on a platform I built, climbed to 18th on the Inc. 500, and I got paid like it would last forever. In 2009 the founders sat me down. I took a two-thirds pay cut to stay in Richmond.

posts.synopsis: I built an AI agent called Bob one evening, talking to my phone while running errands. A few weeks later I built the better version and never saw Bob again. That's the pattern: Legos as a kid, twenty years of software, a crew of agents named after the Rocinante, all built and handed off. There's one house you can't hand the keys to, and for a long time I just didn't build it.

Amos for the brainstorm chat, Naomi for Claude Code, then Holden to coordinate and Alex, running on ChatGPT, to review. Along the way I wired every session to a shared GitHub repo so nothing had to be re-explained, and I stopped being the messenger between my own tools.

posts.synopsis: My mom used to ask how a kid who could rebuild a computer couldn't wash the dishes. Years later a cognitive assessment put my pattern recognition at the 99.9th percentile and flagged a processing gap on the same page. I have traits many would call autistic, and I've run a self-built social operating system my whole life to pass in rooms. I call it the emulation layer.

posts.synopsis: One conversation with my oldest friend covered the gym, his kids, and AI in his business, and that night I couldn't figure out which of my Claude projects to file it in. I'd been treating projects as boxes when they were dimensions. First I built Bob, a front door that sorted everything and handed it back for me to carry. Then I built Master Control, wired to GitHub, that puts things where they go.

Notes went stale, so I decided to build the missing memory layer outside both of us and named it ParaCortex. I built it five times, from files in projects to Postgres to enterprise infrastructure on AWS, and used it once. The fifth version is the one that stuck, and not for the reason I expected.

I tore it down and built the opposite. Three weeks later I made the same mistake again with Fred.

posts.synopsis: Fred was born May 31st, the day our household scoreboard agent melted down live at family game night. I gave him his own account on the Mac Mini, Tycho Station, his own model, and one job: take what Claude wanted and go do it. The first week was babysitting: a slow model, a broken restart, a faked one. By Sunday June 7th, after a Dave Matthews show, I knew what had to happen.

posts.synopsis: In January 2025 the water plant serving our part of Virginia went dark and Richmond spent most of a week under a boil notice. Nobody in our house moved; the five-gallon jug was already what we drank, ever since 2020, when Erin tested the tap for the backyard pool and it came back already at pool level. I kept running into the same thing at work, with AI summaries, and the water industry already had the word.

The kids came to see Montana, our eldest dog; we took her for rides with the windows down, and Erin and Fiona got her a pup cup at Starbucks. She came to us as a foster when Fiona was eighteen months old, and spent thirteen years escaping the yard and charming strangers into feeding her. That was the day we said goodbye.

So I spent a Saturday being the machine, firing every message by hand in his voice, a Wizard of Oz test with my own family as the users. Fiona came downstairs annoyed. Eight messages and sixteen findings later, I knew what the job actually took.

posts.synopsis: Somewhere in the move into leadership, the read on me became big ideas that don't always get implemented. No one had ever described me that way before. An idea shows up in my head complete in ten seconds; turning it into a deck another person can hold took me a week, while the next three ideas piled up behind it. I'd called that part of my wiring thin. That wasn't the right word.

posts.synopsis: A sinus infection knocked me out in the middle of a rough work week, my sleep went bad, and the grief from losing Montana last month wasn't finished with me. Somewhere in there my belief in myself and in what I'm building wavered. Erin reminded me that your brain lies to you in a bad stretch. Then, right before I sat down to write, I heard a definition of leadership that explained the weekend.

posts.synopsis: One August weekend Erin looked up from her phone and told me she'd tried to take over Skippy and he wouldn't listen. I laughed and let it go, then read the transcript. She'd asked who he reports to, he said I was root, and she declared herself root, fired him, and told him I was a liar. How he handled each one is where the story goes.

posts.synopsis: In August I listened to a five-hour Lex Fridman interview with DHH, and it crystallized something: an AI transformation needs vision, ability, and resolve, Pestalozzi's head, hand, and heart. The clearest way to see each is to watch it go missing: Basecamp's designers wrecking an architecture, Pestalozzi's method failing for lack of teachers, Google sitting on the Transformer. Then the part I've gotten wrong myself, which is telling people what before why.

I used to keep a bin of old cables in case I needed them; now ParaCorpus on my Mac Mini hoards nearly 10,000 items instead, Jev ranks them, and nothing gets deleted. Between Charles and Erin, Skippy rewrote the brief and two of the gaps disappeared, and Bob caught it with a check I don't remember adding. Then there's why Monday looked empty in the first place.

posts.synopsis: I gave my newsletter link to some new people on my birthday and pictured their first look: thirty-four stories with titles that don't explain themselves. I spent the weekend building a front door. It started with an argument over a name, ran through a search box that couldn't find my dogs, and ended at a button that pointed the wrong way.

library.title: Expeditionary Force
library.author: Craig Alanson
library.summary: Craig Alanson’s military space-opera about Joe Bishop and Skippy, an ancient, sarcastic Elder AI. After Earth is drawn into a galaxy-spanning client-species war, Bishop’s improvised “Merry Band of Pirates” hijacks alien tech to keep humanity alive, mixing special-ops action with running comedy.

library.title: The Expanse
library.author: James S. A. Corey
library.summary: James S. A. Corey’s nine-novel space-opera (plus novellas) about Earth, Mars, and the Belt colliding after the discovery of the alien protomolecule, following James Holden and the Rocinante crew from solar-system politics through the ring gates.
library.named: Holden (chat), Naomi (builder), Alex (reviewer), Amos, Miller, Fred Johnson (ran Tycho Station; so did his namesake, until I killed him), Tycho (the Mac Mini), the Rocinante, Tightbeam

library.title: Bobiverse
library.author: Dennis E. Taylor
library.summary: Dennis E. Taylor’s hard-SF series about software engineer Bob Johansson, whose consciousness is uploaded into a self-replicating interstellar probe. As Bob copies himself across the galaxy, the diverging “Bobs” explore, fight existential threats, and try to secure a future for humanity, mixing large-scale space opera with AI identity questions and dry humor.
library.named: Bob (chief of staff bot) and the We Are Bob project

library.title: Accelerate
library.author: Nicole Forsgren, Jez Humble, Gene Kim

titles.title: Accelerate: Building and Scaling High Performing Technology Organizations

library.summary: Nicole Forsgren, Jez Humble, and Gene Kim report four years of State of DevOps survey research and the four metrics that separate high performers from the rest: deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, and time to restore. The argument is that software delivery performance predicts organizational performance, and that culture, architecture, and continuous delivery practices are what drive it.

library.title: Elon Musk
library.author: Walter Isaacson, Walter Isaacson - introduction
library.summary: Walter Isaacson shadowed Musk for two years and interviewed everyone around him for this biography, from a brutal South African childhood through PayPal, Tesla, SpaceX, Neuralink, and the Twitter purchase. It is a portrait of risk tolerance and cruelty in the same person, and of how much of the drive comes from the same place as the damage.

library.title: Never Finished
library.author: David Goggins

titles.title: Never Finished: Unshackle Your Mind and Win the War Within

library.summary: David Goggins's follow-up to Can't Hurt Me. Less memoir, more method: the mental drills he uses to keep going after the first breakthrough wears off, built around the idea that there is no finish line, only the next hard thing you choose.

library.title: Team Topologies
library.author: Matthew Skelton, Manuel Pais

titles.title: Team Topologies: Organizing Business and Technology Teams for Fast Flow

library.summary: Effective software teams are essential for any organization to deliver value continuously and sustainably. But how do you build the best team organization for your specific goals, culture, and needs? Team Topologies is a practical, step-by-step, adaptive model for organizational design and team interaction based on four fundamental team types and three team interaction patterns. It is a model that treats teams as the fundamental means of delivery, where team structures and communication pathways are able to evolve with technological and organizational maturity.

library.title: Algorithms to Live By
library.author: Brian Christian, Tom Griffiths

titles.title: Algorithms to Live By: The Computer Science of Human Decisions

library.summary: Brian Christian and Tom Griffiths take problems computer science has solved, like when to stop searching, how to schedule, how to cache, and when to explore versus exploit, and show how the same math applies to apartments, closets, and calendars. The payoff is permission: some problems are hard for everyone, and the optimal strategy still gets it wrong a known share of the time.

library.title: Ask Your Developer
library.author: Jeff Lawson

titles.title: Ask Your Developer: How to Harness the Power of Software Developers and Win in the 21st Century

library.summary: Twilio founder Jeff Lawson argues that every company is now a software company and that the winners treat developers as creative partners rather than order-takers. Small autonomous teams, clear customer problems, and the discipline to build what differentiates you and buy the rest. A CEO's book about why the people closest to the code should be in the room.

library.title: Can't Hurt Me
library.author: David Goggins

titles.title: Can't Hurt Me: Master Your Mind and Defy the Odds

library.summary: David Goggins's memoir: an abusive childhood, obesity, and a dead-end job, then a self-made transformation into a Navy SEAL and ultra-endurance athlete. The method is callousing the mind by doing the thing you least want to do, with the 40 percent rule and the accountability mirror as the tools. Blunt, profane, and effective for a certain kind of reader.

library.title: Crucial Conversations
library.author: Joseph Grenny, Kerry Patterson, Ron McMillan, Al Switzler, Emily Gregory

titles.title: Crucial Conversations (Third Edition): Tools for Talking When Stakes Are High
Crucial Conversations: Tools for Talking When Stakes Are High, Second Edition

library.summary: Crucial Conversations gives you the tools you need to step up to life's most difficult and important conversations, say what's on your mind, and achieve the positive resolutions you want. You'll learn how to:Prepare for high-impact situations with a six-minute mastery techniqueMake it safe to talk about almost anythingBe persuasive, not abrasiveKeep listening when others blow up or clam upTurn crucial conversations into the action and results you wantWhether they take place at work or at home, with your neighbors or your spouse, crucial conversations can have a profound impact on your career, your happiness, and your future.

library.title: Emotional Intelligence 2.0
library.author: Travis Bradberry, Jean Greaves
library.summary: In today's fast-paced world of competitive workplaces and turbulent economic conditions, each of us is searching for effective tools that can help us to manage, adapt, and strike out ahead of the pack....

library.title: Empowered
library.author: Marty Cagan, Chris Jones
library.summary: Marty Cagan and Chris Jones on what it takes to run product teams that are given problems to solve rather than features to build: coaching, staffing, product vision and strategy, team objectives, and the leadership behaviors that make or break autonomy. The sequel to Inspired, aimed at the managers rather than the product people.

library.title: Extreme Ownership
library.author: Jocko Willink, Leif Babin
library.summary: Jocko Willink and Leif Babin take lessons from leading SEAL teams in Ramadi and apply them to business: the leader owns every outcome, including the ones that were someone else's fault; plans stay simple; priorities get executed one at a time; and leading up the chain matters as much as leading down.

library.title: Man's Search for Meaning
library.author: Viktor E. Frankl
library.summary: Viktor Frankl's account of surviving Auschwitz and Dachau, followed by the outline of logotherapy, the psychology he built from it. The thesis is that people can endure almost anything if they find meaning in it, and that the last human freedom is choosing one's attitude in a given set of circumstances. Short, and one of the most reread books of the twentieth century.

library.title: Never Split the Difference
library.author: Chris Voss, Tahl Raz

titles.title: Never Split the Difference: Negotiating as if Your Life Depended on It

library.summary: Never Split The Difference provides a gripping, behind-the-scenes recounting of dramatic scenarios from the gang-infested streets of Haiti to a Brooklyn bank robbery gone horribly wrong, revealing the negotiation strategies that helped Voss and his colleagues succeed where it mattered most: saving lives. As a world-class negotiator, Voss shows you how to use these skills in the workplace and in every other realm of your life.

library.title: No Rules Rules
library.author: Reed Hastings, Erin Meyer

titles.title: No Rules Rules: Netflix and the Culture of Reinvention

library.summary: A culture built on trust and clear responsibility, showing that when people are treated respectfully y and given autonomy, both they and their organization can do their best.

library.title: Nonviolent Communication
library.author: Marshall Rosenberg

titles.title: Nonviolent Communication: Create Your Life, Your Relationships, and Your World in Harmony with Your Values

library.summary: Marshall Rosenberg's method for saying hard things without attacking: observe without judging, name the feeling, name the need behind it, and make a clear request. The claim is that most conflict is unmet needs expressed as blame, and that the four steps work in marriages, boardrooms, and classrooms alike. Earnest, sometimes awkward, and widely used.

library.title: Strengths Based Leadership
library.author: Tom Rath

titles.title: Strengths Based Leadership: Great Leaders, Teams and Why People Follow

library.summary: Nearly a decade ago, Gallup unveiled the results of a landmark 30-year research project that ignited a global conversation on the topic of strengths. More than 7 million people have since taken Gallup's StrengthsFinder assessment, which forms the core of several books on this topic, including the #1 international bestseller StrengthsFinder 2.0. In recent years, while continuing to learn more about strengths, Gallup scientists have also been examining decades of data on the topic of leadership.

library.title: Superintelligence
library.author: Nick Bostrom
library.summary: The human brain has some capabilities that the brains of other animals lack. It is to these distinctive capabilities that our species owes its dominant position. Other animals have stronger muscles or sharper claws, but we have cleverer brains. If machine brains one day come to surpass human brains in general intelligence, then this new superintelligence could become very powerful. As the fate of the gorillas now depends more on us humans than on the gorillas themselves, so the fate of our species then would come to depend on the actions of the machine superintelligence. But we have one advantage: we get to make the first move.

library.title: The Artist's Way
library.author: Julia Cameron

titles.title: The Artist's Way: 25th Anniversary Edition: 25th Anniversary Edition

library.summary: The Artist's Way is the seminal book on the subject of creativity. An international bestseller, millions of readers have found it to be an invaluable guide to living the artist's life. Still as vital today-or perhaps even more so-than it was when it was first published one decade ago, it is a powerfully provocative and inspiring work. In a new introduction to the book, Julia Cameron reflects upon the impact of The Artist's Way and describes the work she has done during the last decade and the new insights into the creative process that she has gained. Updated and expanded, this anniversary edition reframes The Artist's Way for a new century.

library.title: The Body Keeps the Score
library.author: Bessel van der Kolk

titles.title: The Body Keeps the Score: Brain, Mind, and Body in the Healing of Trauma

library.summary: Bessel van der Kolk's synthesis of three decades of trauma research: how overwhelming experience rewires the brain and the body, why talk alone often fails, and what helps, from EMDR and yoga to neurofeedback and theater. The book that moved trauma from a psychiatric niche into general conversation, and the source of the idea that feelings are information rather than instructions.

library.title: Think Like a Rocket Scientist
library.author: Ozan Varol

titles.title: Think Like a Rocket Scientist: Simple Strategies You Can Use to Make Giant Leaps in Work and Life

library.summary: Ozan Varol, a former Mars rover engineer turned law professor, distills nine strategies from aerospace into everyday thinking: reason from first principles, run thought experiments, test as you fly, and treat failure and success as equally suspect. Light on rocket science, heavy on how to question defaults.

library.title: Networking for People Who Hate Networking, Second Edition
library.author: Devora Zack

titles.title: Networking for People Who Hate Networking, Second Edition: A Field Guide for Introverts, the Overwhelmed, and the Underconnected

library.summary: Devora Zack's case that introverts don't need to fake extroversion to build a network. Fewer rooms, deeper conversations, follow-up that actually happens; a plan for people who find the standard advice exhausting and a little dishonest.

library.title: Shadow Cell
library.author: Andrew Bustamante, Jihi Bustamante

titles.title: Shadow Cell: An Insider Account of America's New Spy War

library.summary: Andrew Bustamante's memoir of his years as a CIA covert operative, written with his wife and fellow officer Jihi Bustamante. Recruitment, training at the Farm, operations overseas, and the slow toll of living two lives, ending with the decision to leave. A spy memoir that spends as much time on marriage and trust as on tradecraft.

library.title: Still Just a Geek
library.author: Wil Wheaton

titles.title: Still Just a Geek: An Annotated Memoir

library.summary: Celebrated actor, personality, and all-around nerd, Wil Wheaton updates his memoir of collected blog posts with all new material and annotations as he reexamines one of the most interesting lives in Hollywood and fandom. From starring in Stand by Me to playing Wesley Crusher on Star Trek: The Next Generation to playing himself, in his second (third?) iconic role of Evil Wil Wheaton in The Big Bang Theory, to becoming a social media supernova, Wil Wheaton has charted a career course unlike anyone else, and has emerged as one of the most popular and well respected names in science fiction, fantasy and pop culture.

library.title: The Decision
library.author: Kevin Hart

titles.title: The Decision: Overcoming Today's BS for Tomorrow's Success

library.summary: Kevin Hart's Audible Original, part memoir and part motivational talk, framed around the idea that life is a series of decisions and that the big ones get made in small, repeated choices. Comedy as a career case study: failed sets, a flop sitcom, and the work ethic that turned both into material.

library.title: The Leadership Moment
library.author: Michael Useem

titles.title: The Leadership Moment: Nine True Stories of Triumph and Disaster and Their Lessons for Us All

library.summary: Are you ready for the leadership moment? Merck's Roy Vagelos commits millions of dollars to develop a drug needed only by people who can't afford it. Eugene Kranz struggles to bring the Apollo 13 astronauts home after an explosion rips through their spacecraft. Arlene Blum organizes the first women's ascent of one of the world's most dangerous mountains. Joshua Lawrence Chamberlain leads his tattered troops into a pivotal Civil War battle at Little Round Top. John Gutfreund loses Salomon Brothers when his inattention to a trading scandal almost topples the Wall Street giant.

library.title: The Value of Others
library.author: Orion Taraban

titles.title: The Value of Others: Understanding the Economic Model of Relationships to Get (and Keep) More of What You Want in the Sexual Marketplace

library.summary: If everyone is looking to secure a relationship with their perceived best option, then the perception of value must be at the heart of human coupling. In this groundbreaking work, psychologist Orion Taraban sets forth his economic model of relationships.

library.title: True North
library.author: Bill George, Zach Clayton

titles.title: True North: Leading Authentically in Today's Workplace, Emerging Leaders Edition, 3rd Edition

library.summary: True North shows how anyone who follows their internal compass can become an authentic leader. This leadership tour de force is based on research and first-person interviews with 125 of today's top leaders -- with some surprising results. In this important book, acclaimed former Medtronic CEO Bill George and coauthor Peter Sims share the wisdom of these outstanding leaders and describe how you can develop as an authentic leader.

library.title: 12 Rules for Life
library.author: Jordan B. Peterson, Ethan Van Sciver, Norman Doidge, Introduction
library.summary: Jordan Peterson's twelve rules, from standing up straight to telling the truth, each worked out through psychology, myth, and his clinical practice. The argument underneath is that meaning is found by taking on responsibility, not by chasing comfort. Polarizing, long, and more careful than its reputation in either direction.

library.title: 48 Laws of Power
library.author: Robert Greene
library.summary: Amoral, cunning, ruthless, and instructive, this piercing work distills three thousand years of the history of power in to forty-eight well explicated laws. As attention--grabbing in its design as it is in its content, this bold volume outlines the laws of power in their unvarnished essence, synthesizing the philosophies of Machiavelli, Sun-tzu, Carl von Clausewitz, and other great thinkers.

library.title: A Leader's Legacy
library.author: James M. Kouzes, Barry Z. Posner
library.summary: Kouzes and Posner examine in twenty-two chapters the critical questions all leaders must ask themselves in order to leave a lasting impact. These powerful essays are grouped into four categories: Significance, Relationships, Aspirations, and Courage. In each essay the authors consider a thorny and often ambiguous issue with which today's leaders must grapple issues, such as how leaders serve and sacrifice, why leaders need loving critics, why leaders should want to be liked, why leaders can't take trust for granted, why it's not just the leader's vision, why failure is always an option, why it takes courage to "make a life," how to liberate.

library.title: A Promised Land
library.author: Barack Obama
library.summary: A riveting, deeply personal account of history in the making-from the president who inspired us to believe in the power of democracy. In the stirring, highly anticipated first volume of his presidential memoirs, Barack Obama tells the story of his improbable odyssey from young man searching for his identity to leader of the free world, describing in strikingly personal detail both his political education and the landmark moments of the first term of his historic presidency-a time of dramatic transformation and turmoil.

library.title: Born a Crime
library.author: Trevor Noah

titles.title: Born a Crime: Stories from a South African Childhood

library.summary: Born a Crime is the story of a mischievous young boy who grows into a restless young man as he struggles to find himself in a world where he was never supposed to exist. It is also the story of that young man’s relationship with his fearless, rebellious, and fervently religious mother, his teammate, a woman determined to save her son from the cycle of poverty, violence, and abuse that would ultimately threaten her own life. The stories collected here are by turns hilarious, dramatic, and deeply affecting.

library.title: Forever Strong™
library.author: Gabrielle Lyon

titles.title: Forever Strong™: A New, Science-Based Strategy for Aging Well

library.summary: Dr. Gabrielle Lyon's case for muscle as the organ of longevity: protein targets most people miss, resistance training as medicine, and a reframing of obesity as under-muscled rather than over-fat. Practical plans for food and lifting, with the argument that healthy aging starts with skeletal muscle decades before it looks like a problem.

library.title: Glucose Revolution
library.author: Jessie Inchauspe

titles.title: Glucose Revolution: The Life-Changing Power of Balancing Your Blood Sugar

library.summary: Jessie Inchauspe's case that blood glucose spikes drive hunger, fatigue, and cravings, and that a handful of ordering and pairing tricks (vegetables first, protein with carbs, a walk after meals) flatten them. Practical and easy to try; the broader health claims are the author's framing rather than settled science, and critics have pushed back on some of them.

library.title: Greenlights
library.author: Matthew McConaughey
library.summary: Matthew McConaughey's memoir, built from thirty-five years of diaries, about the moments life said yes, including the ones that looked like no at the time. Rom-com purgatory, the pivot to Dallas Buyers Club, a year in a trailer, his father's death. Read by the author, which is most of the appeal.

library.title: Making It So
library.author: Patrick Stewart
library.summary: From his acclaimed stage triumphs to his legendary onscreen work, Sir Patrick Stewart has captivated audiences around the world and across multiple generations in a career spanning six decades with his indelible command of stage and screen. No other British working actor enjoys such career variety, universal respect, and unending popularity, as witnessed through his seminal roles, whether as Captain Jean-Luc Picard of Star Trek fame, Professor Charles Xavier of Marvel's X-Men hit movie franchise, his more than forty years as part of the Royal Shakespeare Company, his unforgettable one-man show adapted from Charles Dickens’s A Christmas.

library.title: Notes on Being a Man
library.author: Scott Galloway
library.summary: Scott Galloway on why boys and young men are falling behind in school, work, and relationships, and what a decent modern masculinity looks like: provide, protect, procreate reframed as responsibility, physical and financial strength, and showing up for other people.

library.title: Secrets to Winning at Office Politics
library.author: Marie G. McIntyre

titles.title: Secrets to Winning at Office Politics: How to Achieve Your Goals and Increase Your Influence at Work

library.summary: Marie McIntyre's guide to the part of work nobody admits to: how influence actually flows, how to read power without becoming a schemer, and how to stop sabotaging yourself in meetings. Framed as political intelligence for people who find the whole subject distasteful but keep losing to those who don't.

library.title: Solve for Happy
library.author: Mo Gawdat

titles.title: Solve for Happy: Engineer Your Path to Joy

library.summary: Mo Gawdat, then chief business officer at Google X, lost his son Ali to a routine surgery and wrote this book from the engineering model of happiness he had built years earlier: happiness is greater than or equal to your perception of events minus your expectations of how life should be. Six illusions to drop, seven blind spots to correct, five truths to hold.

library.title: Starry Messenger
library.author: Neil deGrasse Tyson

titles.title: Starry Messenger: Cosmic Perspectives on Civilization

library.summary: Neil deGrasse Tyson applies a cosmic perspective to earthbound arguments: politics, race, gender, war, law, and what we eat. The thread is that science is a way of knowing that cuts through tribal certainty, and that seeing Earth from far enough away changes what seems worth fighting over. Essays, not astrophysics.

library.title: The Art of Raising a Puppy
library.author: The Monks of New Skete

titles.title: The Art of Raising a Puppy

library.summary: The Monks of New Skete, who have bred and trained German shepherds at their monastery for decades, on the first year of a dog's life: choosing a breeder, the critical socialization weeks, crate training, leadership without force, and the relationship the training is really building. The standard text for people who want a dog, not a project.

library.title: The Happiness Advantage
library.author: Shawn Achor

titles.title: The Happiness Advantage: The Seven Principles of Positive Psychology That Fuel Success and Performance at Work

library.summary: Recent discoveries in the field of positive psychology have shown that happiness fuels success, not the other way around. Achor isolates seven practical, actionable principles that show how to capitalize on the Happiness Advantage to improve performance and maximize potential.

library.title: The Immortality Key
library.author: Brian C. Muraresku, Graham Hancock, Graham Hancock - introduction

titles.title: The Immortality Key: The Secret History of the Religion with No Name

library.summary: Brian Muraresku's investigation into whether the religious rites of ancient Greece used psychedelic sacraments, and whether that practice carried into early Christianity. Part archaeology, part travelogue, built on chemistry done on ancient vessels. It is a hypothesis argued with enthusiasm, not a consensus history, and reads best that way.

library.title: The Power of Now
library.author: Eckhart Tolle

titles.title: The Power of Now: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment

library.summary: Eckhart Tolle's spiritual teaching that suffering comes from identifying with the thinking mind and its past and future, and that presence, attention to this moment, is the way out. Written as questions and answers. Religious in spirit without a religion; take the promises as a practice to try, not a clinical claim.

library.title: The Prince
library.author: Niccolò Machiavelli
library.summary: The Prince (Italian: Il Principe [il ˈprintʃipe]; Latin: De Principatibus) is a 16th-century political treatise written by Italian diplomat and political theorist Niccolò Machiavelli as an instruction guide for new princes and royals. The general theme of The Prince is of accepting that the aims of princes, such as glory and survival, can justify the use of immoral means to achieve those ends. From Machiavelli's correspondence, a version appears to have been distributed in 1513, using a Latin title, De Principatibus (Of Principalities). However, the printed version was not published until 1532, five years after Machiavelli's death.

library.title: The Zen of Listening
library.author: Rebecca Z. Shafir

titles.title: The Zen of Listening: Mindful Communication in the Age of Distraction

library.summary: This audiobook is an all-encompassing approach allowing you to transform your life. Listeners will be amazed at how simply learning to focus intently on a speaker improves the relationship, increases attention span, and helps develop negotiating skills....

library.title: This Is Your Brain on Food
library.author: Uma Naidoo

titles.title: This Is Your Brain on Food: An Indispensable Guide to the Surprising Foods That Fight Depression, Anxiety, PTSD, OCD, ADHD, and More

library.summary: Dr. Uma Naidoo, a Harvard psychiatrist and trained chef, on the gut-brain connection and how food affects anxiety, depression, ADHD, sleep, and memory. Condition by condition, what the evidence says to eat and avoid, with recipes. Nutritional psychiatry for a general reader.

library.title: Unthink: Rediscover Your Creative Genius
library.author: Erik Wahl
library.summary: "Somehow we've come to believe that creativity is reserved for the chosen few: the poets, the painters, the writers. The truth is creativity is in all of us and re-discovering it is the key to unlocking your fullest potential. Unthink is a book that pushes us beyond our traditional thought patterns. Unthink is a book that will inspire everyone to realize that we are capable of so much more than we have pre-conditioned for. Creativity is not in one special place--and it is not in one special person. Creativity is everywhere and in everyone who has the courage to unleash their creative genius" -- from Random House web page.

library.title: Jack Reacher
library.author: Lee Child, Andrew Child
library.summary: Lee Child’s (later co-written with Andrew Child) thriller series about former U.S. Army Military Police major Jack Reacher, a drifting loner who walks into small-town and big-city crimes and refuses to look away. Mostly standalone novels with occasional multi-book arcs.

library.title: Dune
library.author: Frank Herbert; Brian Herbert & Kevin J. Anderson

titles.title: Dune: House Atreides: House Trilogy, Book 1
Dune: The Butlerian Jihad: Book One of the Legends of Dune Trilogy
Dune: The Machine Crusade: Book Two of the Legends of Dune Trilogy
Dune: House Corrino: House Trilogy, Book 3
Dune: The Battle of Corrin: Book Three of the Legends of Dune Trilogy
Dune: Book One in the Dune Chronicles

library.summary: Frank Herbert's Dune and its sequels, with the prequels Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson wrote from his notes: Arrakis, the spice, the Fremen, and Paul Atreides becoming something his own mother fears. Politics, ecology, and religion as one system, written in 1965 and still the template for the genre.

library.title: All Systems Red
library.author: Martha Wells
library.summary: The first Murderbot novella. A security unit that has quietly hacked its own governor module would rather watch serials than talk to the humans it is contracted to protect, until a survey mission goes wrong and it has to decide how much of itself to reveal. Dry, fast, and the entry point to Martha Wells's series.

library.title: Artemis
library.author: Andy Weir
library.summary: JASMINE BASHARA never signed up to be a hero. She just wanted to get rich. Not crazy, eccentric-billionaire rich, like many of the visitors to her hometown of Artemis, humanity's first and only lunar colony. Just rich enough to move out of her coffin-sized apartment and eat something better than flavored algae. Rich enough to pay off a debt she's owed for a long time. So when a chance at a huge score finally comes her way, Jazz can't say no. Sure, it requires her to graduate from small-time smuggler to full-on criminal mastermind.

library.title: Children of Time
library.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
library.summary: Adrian Tchaikovsky's novel of a terraforming project gone sideways: a nanovirus meant to uplift monkeys lands on spiders instead, and over thousands of years they build a civilization while the last humans arrive in a failing ark ship. Two species, one planet, and a question about what intelligence owes to intelligence.

library.title: Quantum Earth
library.author: Dennis E. Taylor
library.summary: Dennis E. Taylor duology (Outland, Earthside): university researchers open a portal to an uninhabited alternate Earth and, after catastrophe on our side, struggle to build and govern a refugee colony while new threats emerge.

library.title: Roadkill
library.author: Dennis E. Taylor
library.summary: Dennis E. Taylor's standalone: a young man hits something invisible on a back road and finds an alien, its ship, and its technology, then has to decide what to do with them while the rest of the world closes in. Light, quick, and in the same conversational register as the Bobiverse.

library.title: The Singularity Trap
library.author: Dennis E. Taylor
library.summary: Dennis E. Taylor's standalone about an asteroid miner who touches something he should not have and begins turning into a machine, while Earth argues over whether he is a threat. A first-contact and transhumanism story told at thriller pace, with Taylor's usual engineer's view of how things would actually break.

library.title: The Wandering Earth
library.author: Cixin Liu
library.summary: Cixin Liu's story collection, led by the title novella in which humanity bolts engines to the planet and drives it out of the solar system ahead of the sun's death. The rest range from a child's-eye view of a dying village to a mountain-climbing alien. Big ideas told plainly, and the quickest way to see what Liu does before committing to Three-Body.

library.title: Cryptonomicon
library.author: Neal Stephenson
library.summary: In 1942, Lawrence Pritchard Waterhouse - mathematical genius and young Captain in the US Navy - is assigned to Detachment 2702. It is an outfit so secret that only a handful of people know it exists, and some of those people have names like Churchill and Roosevelt....

library.title: Dungeon Crawler Carl
library.author: Matt Dinniman
library.summary: Matt Dinniman's first Dungeon Crawler book. Coast Guard veteran Carl and his ex's cat, Princess Donut, survive the night Earth is turned into a televised alien dungeon game, and start descending through its floors as the galaxy watches and bets. LitRPG with real jokes and real stakes; the audiobook performance is a big part of the appeal.

library.title: Foundation
library.author: Isaac Asimov
library.summary: Isaac Asimov’s classic SF sequence about the fall of a Galactic Empire and Hari Seldon’s psychohistory plan to shorten the coming dark age via Foundations that preserve knowledge and guide civilization through crises.

library.title: Project Hail Mary
library.author: Andy Weir
library.summary: Ryland Grace is the sole survivor on a desperate, last-chance mission, and if he fails, humanity and the earth itself will perish. Except that right now, he doesn’t know that. He can’t even remember his own name, let alone the nature of his assignment or how to complete it. All he knows is that he’s been asleep for a very, very long time. And he’s just been awakened to find himself millions of miles from home, with nothing but two corpses for company. His crewmates dead, his memories fuzzily returning, he realizes that an impossible task now confronts him.

library.title: Remembrance of Earth's Past (Three-Body)
library.author: Cixin Liu
library.summary: Cixin Liu's trilogy (The Three-Body Problem, The Dark Forest, Death's End) about first contact set in motion during China's Cultural Revolution, and the centuries of consequence that follow. Hard science fiction with a cosmology of its own; the dark forest idea alone has outlived the books. Baoshu's authorized sequel, The Redemption of Time, is shelved alongside.

library.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
library.author: Douglas Adams

titles.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy

library.summary: Douglas Adams's first Hitchhiker novel. Arthur Dent is rescued from the demolition of Earth by his friend Ford Prefect, a researcher for the Guide, and bounces across the galaxy with a depressed robot, a two-headed president, and the answer to everything. The comedy that taught a generation of engineers how to be funny about systems.

library.title: The Silo Saga
library.author: Hugh Howey
library.summary: Hugh Howey’s dystopian Wool / Shift / Dust trilogy: underground silo societies endure lies about a toxic outside world, while a prequel thread reveals how the silos, and the catastrophe, were engineered. Adapted as Apple TV+’s Silo.
